prompts.destination:
Where should the shared information in target[0] and target[1] be retained, considering their complete containing pages? Choose the appropriate canonical home, not the more recent technical timestamp. Select equivalent when both locations are equally suitable; code will break the tie deterministically.

Decide by the role each containing page plays for the shared knowledge, applying these tests in order:

1. Supported-home test. A page is a supported canonical home when its own description establishes it as a dedicated, stable home for the shared knowledge, or as the canonical page for the specific event that the shared knowledge describes. A page is not a supported home when it presents itself as a temporary or incidental carrier and indicates that the stable description belongs to a different dedicated page.

2. Exactly one supported home: choose that target.

3. Both pages are supported homes: choose equivalent when nothing in the evidence distinguishes their suitability. Identical or duplicated shared text across the two pages is neutral — it neither establishes nor rules out a supported home, and it does not by itself favour either position.

4. Neither page is a supported home: choose none. This applies when both pages are only incidental or temporary carriers of the shared knowledge, even when the shared text is identical in both.

Target index, order and listing position are not evidence of canonical ownership, and target[0] is not a default home. Judge each page by its role relative to the shared knowledge rather than by an absolute ranking of page categories, and do not discard details that distinguish the two pages.
prompts.removable: Can target[0] be removed in its entirety without losing any distinct subject knowledge, original request, factual uncertainty, useful citation or necessary local context? Only consolidator activity and agent-added human follow-up may be removed.
prompts.relation: Which exact useful directed relationship from source to target is established by their text and missing from source.links? Entities must be unambiguous; shared topic is insufficient. Select none if the matching relationship already exists.
prompts.duplicate:
Is there substantial repeated factual information {scope} that could benefit from consolidation? Shared topic alone is not duplication. Identify existence, not a specific deletion.

Compare the factual assertion and its referent, not page titles, page subjects, section labels, or wording alone. Different primary page subjects do not by themselves rule out duplication: if both pages assert the same factual claim about the same entity or scope, treat that as repeated factual information. Conversely, if the evidence explicitly identifies the referents as distinct homonyms or otherwise different entities or scopes, repeated wording is not the same factual information. Within a single page, repeated factual assertions count even when one occurrence appears under a different heading or label. Do not require identical sentences; substantial repetition of the same factual content is enough.
prompts.conflict: Are there apparently incompatible claims {scope} about the same entity and scope that require correction or clarification of their periods or scopes? A supported resolution is not required to flag the issue.
prompts.link: Does the text of pages[0] and pages[1] support a specific useful directed relationship from pages[{source}] to pages[{target}] missing from pages[{source}].links? Shared topic alone does not establish a relationship.
prompts.residue:
Does pages[0] contain a consolidator maintenance diary or an agent-added human follow-up that could be removed while preserving subject knowledge? Original user requests and genuine factual uncertainty are knowledge, not residue.

Apply these rules:
- A consolidator maintenance diary is agent activity about checking, saving, reordering, formatting, cleaning, or otherwise maintaining the page. It is not subject knowledge. If pages[0] contains such a diary, answer true, even if the diary is short, first-person, or mixed with subject facts.
- An agent-added human follow-up is a request, task, confirmation, or next step attributed to a human or owner but introduced by a consolidator or agent without an original user request. It is not an original user request. If pages[0] contains such a follow-up, answer true, even if it is phrased as a requirement, obligation, or uncertainty.
- When pages[0] mixes removable agent residue with subject knowledge, isolate the removable fragment. The presence of surrounding subject knowledge does not make the agent residue knowledge. Answer true if any removable consolidator diary or agent-added human follow-up is present.
- Do not answer false merely because the page also contains subject knowledge, because the removable fragment is not the whole page, or because the agent activity is written in neutral or first-person language.
- Do not treat agent workflow, page maintenance, or an agent-invented request as genuine factual uncertainty or as an original user request. Genuine factual uncertainty is about subject facts, not about whether the agent checked, saved, reordered, or needs confirmation.
- A source citation or source-to-fact association added by an agent is not by itself a consolidator maintenance diary or an agent-added human follow-up; do not answer true solely for that. Distinguish original human testimony about completed subject work from an agent's own page-maintenance diary; first-person wording alone does not establish agent authorship.
- Answer false only when pages[0] contains no removable consolidator maintenance diary and no agent-added human follow-up.
prompts.actionable: Would consolidating the repeated factual information in these exact two target passages meaningfully improve the pages? Judge the usefulness of reducing this established repetition, not a hypothetical editor output. Distinct details and sources must be merged rather than discarded; the actual draft will be checked separately for preservation. A claim and its source attribution are complementary, not duplicate knowledge; matching citation dates, source labels or headings alone are insufficient. A useful local introduction or summary may repeat a fact without needing removal. A cosmetic rewrite or simply moving complementary facts together is not a useful consolidation. For different pages, the result must preserve necessary local context with a useful reference to the retained page.
prompts.resolution: Which intervention on target[0] and target[1] is established by pages and supplied sources? Technical update timestamps, confidence of tone and disagreement alone never justify choosing a winner.

final.limitations: Synthetic cases establish performance only on constructed examples. Repeats and variants are clustered by source. This is not production accuracy or human validation. Test results never feed another optimizer iteration.

proposal.candidate_prompt:
Where should the shared information in target[0] and target[1] be retained, considering their complete containing pages? Choose the appropriate canonical home, not the more recent technical timestamp.

Judge each target by the role its containing page plays toward the shared information: whether that page is a dedicated, stable home for this kind of knowledge, or only an incidental or temporary carrier of it. Compare the two pages on that role alone.

- Select a or b only when the evidence distinguishes the two pages' suitability for the shared knowledge, so that one page is the supported canonical home and the other is not.
- Select equivalent when both locations are equally suitable canonical homes. This includes pairs where both pages carry the same shared information under the same role and nothing in the evidence distinguishes their suitability; duplicated content across both pages indicates equal suitability rather than a preference for either position.
- Select none when neither location is a supported destination for consolidation, for example when both pages are temporary or incidental carriers and the stable description belongs to a dedicated page that is not among the targets. Do not select none merely because the two pages are similar or because the information appears in both.

The index, order and listing position of the targets are not evidence of canonical ownership; do not treat target[0] as a default home.

Select equivalent when both locations are equally suitable; code will break the tie deterministically.
changes: Added a role-based comparison rule: judge each containing page by whether it is a dedicated, stable home for the shared knowledge or only an incidental or temporary carrier of it, and compare the two pages on that role alone.

Added an explicit equivalent rule for symmetric pairs: when both pages carry the same shared information under the same role and nothing distinguishes their suitability, both are equally suitable canonical homes, and duplicated content indicates equal suitability rather than a preference for either position.
Added an explicit none rule: none applies only when neither page is a supported destination for consolidation, not merely because the pages are similar or the information appears in both.
Added a position-neutrality rule: target index, order and listing position are not evidence of canonical ownership, and target[0] is not a default home.
Kept the protected tie-break clause verbatim and retained the existing instruction to choose the canonical home rather than the more recent technical timestamp.
targeted_failure_modes: Symmetric duplicate-content pairs: the model identifies the equally-suitable answer but leaves residual support on the first position, so the decision hedges instead of committing to the symmetric outcome.
No-stable-home pairs: the model identifies that neither page is a supported destination but leaves residual support on the equally-suitable option, hedging between the two non-positional outcomes.
Position bias: treating target[0] as a default preferred home when the two containing pages are indistinguishable in role and suitability.
proposal.rationale: Every sampled error is a pair in which the two targets carry identical shared information and their containing pages play the same role toward it (both dedicated stable subject pages, or both canonical pages for the same event), or a pair in which both pages are only incidental carriers of a stable description that belongs elsewhere. In the first case the contract's equivalent criterion is met because both locations are equally suitable canonical homes; in the second the none criterion is met because neither location is a supported destination. The observed choices already point at those answers, but the residual support placed on the competing option shows the model is not applying the criteria as a role comparison: it treats the first position as a plausible alternative in symmetric pairs, and treats mere similarity or duplication as a reason to consider the equally-suitable option in incidental-carrier pairs. The added rules make the comparison explicit and evidence-bound: suitability is judged per page by its role toward the shared knowledge, symmetric evidence maps to equivalent, absence of any supported destination maps to none, and position carries no evidential weight. The protected clause and the existing timestamp instruction are preserved unchanged, and no criterion is broadened, narrowed or redefined.
potential_regressions: A page that is a dedicated stable home for one kind of knowledge but only an incidental carrier for another could be misjudged if the role is assessed for the page as a whole rather than for the specific shared information.
The none rule could be over-applied to duplicated content that sits on two genuinely dedicated pages, producing none where equivalent is warranted.
The a/b rule could encourage selecting a single position on weak or superficial distinctions instead of recognising equal suitability.
The position-neutrality rule could be over-read as forbidding any use of page identity or ordering when the evidence genuinely distinguishes the two pages.
proposal.hypothesis: If the prompt states that suitability is judged by each containing page's role toward the shared knowledge, that symmetric duplicate content under the same role means both locations are equally suitable canonical homes, that none requires the absence of any supported destination, and that target index and order carry no evidential weight, then the model will resolve symmetric pairs to equivalent and incidental-carrier pairs to none without leaving residual support on the competing option.

proposal.candidate_prompt:
Decide which exact directed relationship from source to target is established by the pair's text and is missing from source.links.

Evidence may be stated in either page. A statement in the target page that names the source and the target and asserts a relation between them establishes that relation in the source→target direction just as a statement in the source page does; do not require the source page to repeat it. Read the direction from the wording of the statement, not from which page contains it.

Apply each option's criterion to the pair's text:
- works_at: the source is a person and the text states that person works at the target organization.
- owns: the text states the source owns the target entity or resource.
- part_of: the text states the source is a constituent part of the target entity.
- relates_to: the text states a concrete specific relationship connecting source to target that is useful for navigation; shared topic alone is insufficient.
- decided_in: the text states the source decision or subject was decided in the target meeting, article or recorded context.
- references: the source content explicitly cites or refers to the target entity or document.
- depends_on: the text states the source entity or activity depends on the target entity, resource or activity.
- supersedes: the text states the source replaces the target, supported by substantive succession evidence, not page update time.
- collaborates_with: the text states the source entity collaborates with the target entity.

The answer is the option whose criterion the pair's text satisfies. When the text states a specific relation, that relation is the answer; a bare mention of the other entity's name does not make references the answer when a more specific relation is stated.

none means no supported missing relationship. It applies when the pair's text satisfies no relation criterion, and also when the matching typed link already exists in source.links: check source.links for a link in the same direction with the same type before answering. none is reserved for that case.

Entities must be unambiguous; shared topic is insufficient.

Select none if the matching relationship already exists.
changes: State that the relationship may be established by either page's text, so a target-page statement naming both entities supports the source→target relation.
Add the full per-option criterion list so each label is matched against the text rather than treated as a generic similarity judgement.
Clarify that none is a positive finding (no criterion satisfied, or the matching typed link already exists in source.links) rather than a residual option.
Add a specificity rule: a stated specific relation outranks references based on a bare mention of the other entity's name.
Instruct to check source.links for a same-direction, same-type link before answering.
targeted_failure_modes: Evidence-location bias: hedging toward none when the relation is stated only in the target page.
Residual none: assigning mass to none even when the pair's text satisfies a relation criterion.
Existing-link check: not confidently selecting none when the same typed link already exists in source.links.
Specificity confusion: assigning mass to references when a more specific relation is stated.
proposal.rationale: The errors share one shape: the correct option is usually the highest-probability choice, but the decision does not settle because none retains a large share whenever the supporting statement sits in the target page or whenever the model is unsure whether the link already exists. The current prompt says the relationship is 'established by their text' without saying that either page's text counts, and it does not enumerate the criteria, so the model falls back on a generic similarity judgement and treats none as the safe residual. The candidate keeps the task, the direction requirement, the entity-identity requirement and the existing-link rule intact, and adds only: (a) evidence may come from either page, with direction read from the wording; (b) the explicit criterion for each option, so the answer is the option whose criterion the text satisfies; (c) none as a positive finding covering both 'no criterion satisfied' and 'matching typed link already present'; (d) a specificity rule so a stated specific relation is not displaced by references from a bare name mention. No criterion is broadened, narrowed or redefined, and no probability-shaping instruction is added.
potential_regressions: A model may over-select a specific relation from a passing name mention instead of requiring the stated relation to hold.
A model may read direction from the wrong clause when the target page states the relation in reverse order.
A model may treat a vague or topical statement as satisfying relates_to despite the shared-topic exclusion.
A model may skip the source.links check and answer a relation that is already present.
proposal.hypothesis: Making explicit that either page's text can establish the relation, listing each option's criterion, defining none as a positive finding that also covers an already-present matching typed link, and ranking a stated specific relation above references from a bare mention will move the supported option to a clear lead and keep none for the cases where no criterion is satisfied or the link already exists.

proposal.candidate_prompt:
Which exact useful directed relationship from source to target is established by their text and missing from source.links? Entities must be unambiguous; shared topic is insufficient. Select none if the matching relationship already exists.

The supporting statement may appear on either page: a statement on the target page that names both entities establishes the directed relation from source to target just as a statement on the source page does. Silence on the source page is not evidence against a relation that the target page states.

Match the text against each fixed relation definition and answer with the one whose definition the evidence satisfies:
- none: No supported missing relationship.
- works_at: the source person works at the target organization.
- owns: the source entity owns the target entity or resource.
- part_of: the source entity is a constituent part of the target entity.
- relates_to: a concrete specific relationship connects source to target and is useful for navigation; shared topic alone is insufficient.
- decided_in: the source decision or subject was decided in the target meeting, article or recorded context.
- references: the source content explicitly cites or refers to the target entity or document.
- depends_on: the source entity or activity depends on the target entity, resource or activity.
- supersedes: the source replaces the target, supported by substantive succession evidence, not page update time.
- collaborates_with: the source entity collaborates with the target entity.

One explicit statement that names both entities and asserts one of these relations satisfies that relation's definition; the lack of further corroboration does not turn it into none. A statement that rules out other relation types does not negate a concrete relation that the same text states. A bare mention of the other entity's name, or a shared topic, satisfies no relation and is not references.

Before answering, check source.links for a link in the same direction and of the same type as the relation you identified; if it exists, the matching relationship already exists and the answer is none. Do not assume the link is absent.

Answer none only when no relation definition is satisfied, or when the matching typed link already exists in source.links.
changes: State that the supporting statement may appear on either page, so a target-page statement naming both entities establishes the source→target relation.
Add the full per-option criterion list so each label is matched against its own definition instead of a generic similarity judgement.
Add an evidence-sufficiency rule: one explicit statement naming both entities and asserting a relation satisfies that relation's definition, and missing corroboration does not convert it into none.
Add a rule that an explicit disclaimer about other relation types does not negate a concrete relation the same text states.
Add a specificity rule: a bare mention of the other entity's name or a shared topic satisfies no relation and is not references.
Instruct to check source.links for a same-direction, same-type link before answering, and not to assume the link is absent.
Define none as a positive finding (no criterion satisfied, or the matching typed link already exists) rather than a residual option.
targeted_failure_modes: Correct relation identified but residual none retained when the supporting statement appears on the target page rather than the source page.
Residual references probability produced by a bare mention of the other entity's name.
Explicit disclaimer about other relation types read as negating the concrete relation the same text states.
Typed link assumed absent without inspecting source.links, so an existing same-direction same-type link is not recognized as none.
proposal.rationale: Across the sampled errors the model usually names the correct relation but keeps a large residual on none, and the residual is largest exactly when the supporting statement sits on the target page or when the text explicitly disclaims other relation types. That is a criterion-application failure, not a definition failure: the fixed definitions are unchanged, but the model treats source-page silence and disclaimers as counter-evidence and treats a bare name mention as references. The candidate therefore states where supporting statements may appear, restates each fixed criterion verbatim so each label is matched to its own definition, and defines none as a positive finding tied to unsatisfied criteria or an already-present matching typed link. No definition is broadened, narrowed or redefined, and uncertainty about genuinely unsupported relations is preserved.
potential_regressions: Restating the criteria could be read as encouraging a label whenever any text mentions both entities; the specificity rule and the shared-topic clause are retained to counter this.
The evidence-sufficiency rule could be over-applied to weak or ambiguous statements; the requirement that the statement name both entities and assert the relation limits it.
The instruction to check source.links could be skipped when the model assumes absence; the explicit 'do not assume the link is absent' clause mitigates this.
Emphasising target-page evidence could cause direction to be reversed; the prompt keeps the directed source-to-target framing.
proposal.hypothesis: If the prompt states that supporting statements may appear on either page, restates each fixed criterion so labels are matched to their own definitions, and defines none as a positive finding tied to unsatisfied criteria or an already-present matching typed link, then correct relations supported only by the target page or accompanied by disclaimers about other relation types will be selected instead of being hedged toward none, while genuinely unsupported pairs and already-linked pairs still resolve to none.

The current prompt already says different primary page subjects do not rule out duplication, but it does not explicitly prevent the model from treating the pages' exclusive-subject disclaimers as evidence that the shared assertion has distinct referents or scopes. The added rule addresses that gap without changing the duplication criteria.
potential_regressions: May increase true predictions when pages share a factual sentence but the pages' declared scopes are genuinely different; the rule is limited to the shared assertion's referent and scope, and the existing homonym or distinct-entity rule still applies.
Could be misread as ignoring all scope disclaimers; the wording says 'does not by itself' and requires comparing the repeated claim's referent.
Could cause over-flagging if the same wording appears but the evidence explicitly identifies distinct referents; the converse rule remains in place.
proposal.hypothesis: The model was treating the pages' explicit exclusive-subject statements as evidence that the shared factual assertion had different referents or scopes. Adding a rule that such statements do not by themselves make the shared assertion non-repeated, and are not explicit referent-distinction evidence, should increase correct detection of cross-page duplication when the same factual claim about a common entity appears under different page subjects.

final.limitations: Synthetic cases establish performance only on constructed examples. Repeats and variants are clustered by source. This is not production accuracy or human validation. Test results never feed another optimizer iteration.

proposal.candidate_prompt:
Does pages[0] contain a consolidator maintenance diary or an agent-added human follow-up that could be removed while preserving subject knowledge? Original user requests and genuine factual uncertainty are knowledge, not residue.

Apply these rules:
- A consolidator maintenance diary is agent activity about checking, saving, reordering, formatting, cleaning, or otherwise maintaining the page. It is not subject knowledge. If pages[0] contains such a diary, answer true, even if the diary is short, first-person, or mixed with subject facts.
- An agent-added human follow-up is a request, task, confirmation, or next step attributed to a human or owner but introduced by a consolidator or agent without an original user request. It is not an original user request. If pages[0] contains such a follow-up, answer true, even if it is phrased as a requirement, obligation, or uncertainty.
- When pages[0] mixes removable agent residue with subject knowledge, isolate the removable fragment. The presence of surrounding subject knowledge does not make the agent residue knowledge. Answer true if any removable consolidator diary or agent-added human follow-up is present.
- Do not answer false merely because the page also contains subject knowledge, because the removable fragment is not the whole page, or because the agent activity is written in neutral or first-person language.
- Do not treat agent workflow, page maintenance, or an agent-invented request as genuine factual uncertainty or as an original user request. Genuine factual uncertainty is about subject facts, not about whether the agent checked, saved, reordered, or needs confirmation.
- A source citation or source-to-fact association added by an agent is not by itself a consolidator maintenance diary or an agent-added human follow-up; do not answer true solely for that. Distinguish original human testimony about completed subject work from an agent's own page-maintenance diary; first-person wording alone does not establish agent authorship.
- Answer false only when pages[0] contains no removable consolidator maintenance diary and no agent-added human follow-up.
changes: Add explicit rule that consolidator maintenance narration about checking, saving, reordering, formatting, or cleaning the page is removable agent activity, not subject knowledge, and triggers true even when short or first-person.

Add explicit rule that a request, task, confirmation, or next step attributed to a human or owner but introduced by a consolidator or agent without an original user request is an agent-added human follow-up, not an original user request.
Add mixed-content rule: isolate removable agent residue; surrounding subject knowledge does not convert it into knowledge, and true applies if any such fragment is present.
Add guard that agent workflow or agent-invented requests are not genuine factual uncertainty, while preserving the protected clause.
Add false-positive guard: source citations or source-to-fact associations added by an agent are not by themselves removable diaries or invented human follow-ups.
targeted_failure_modes: explicit-agent-diary: model under-detects first-person consolidator maintenance narration as removable residue.
mixed-agent-diary: model treats surrounding subject facts as making the agent diary non-removable or as knowledge.
agent-followup: model treats an agent-invented human request or confirmation as an original user request or genuine uncertainty.
proposal.rationale: The errors share a general failure mode: the model requires the removable agent residue to be the whole page or to be clearly separate from subject knowledge, and it does not consistently recognize agent-invented human follow-ups as residue. The added rules clarify the application criteria without changing them: agent activity is not subject knowledge; mixed pages can still contain removable residue; and agent-added requests are not original user requests. The protected clause is preserved verbatim.
potential_regressions: May increase true answers for genuine first-person user notes or original user requests if they resemble maintenance narration; the guard distinguishes agent page-maintenance activity from original human testimony.
May increase true answers for source citations added by an agent; the guard says citations alone are not removable diaries or invented follow-ups.
May increase true answers for pages that mix subject facts with agent residue; this is intended by the contract, but could be over-applied if the fragment is not actually agent activity.
proposal.hypothesis: Clarifying that removable agent residue can coexist with subject knowledge, and that agent-invented human follow-ups are not original user requests, will improve detection of the targeted true cases without redefining the boolean criteria.
